e.etymology: Taken from Dasani, the bottled water brand Coca-Cola launched in 1999. The brand name was invented for the product and has no meaning in any language.
From Hebrew Yefet, the name of one of Noah's three sons. Its origin is uncertain; tradition ties it to a word for enlarge, from the blessing in Genesis 9:27, or to one for fair.

A name with several readings: a spelling of Kieran (Irish Ciaran, little dark one) or of Indian Kiran (ray of light), and the Japanese word for the qilin, a mythical hooved creature, and for the giraffe.
A respelling of Jace, which began as a short form of Jason, Greek for healer, and as a spelling-out of the initials J. C.
A modern American coinage, Jaylee respelled: Jay joined to the -lee ending of Kaylee and Hailee. It has no meaning of its own.
A modern American name, a form of Damani, in the family of Imani, Amani and Armani. Its meaning is not established.
A modern American name in the pattern of Zariyah, Mariah and Taliyah. It has no established meaning.
A Turkish name from Arabic karam, nobility, generosity and kindness. Kerem and Asli is one of the classic love stories of Turkish folk literature.
A modern American coinage that joins the Zy- of Zyaire to the -mir sound of Amir and Jahmir. It has no meaning of its own.
A spelling of Bodie or Bodhi. Bodie is a surname and a California gold-rush ghost town; Bodhi is the Sanskrit and Buddhist word for awakening or enlightenment.
A respelling of Carter, an English occupational surname for someone who hauled goods by cart.
An Italian elaboration of Livia, the feminine of Livius, an old Roman family name borne by the historian Livy and by Livia, wife of the emperor Augustus.
A modern American coinage in the style of Ryder, Ryker, Tyler and Kyler, first recorded in the 2000s.
The flower names Lily and Rose written as one word. The hyphenated form Lily-Rose is more common, especially in Britain and France.
namesakes: Lily-Rose Depp (actress, daughter of Johnny Depp)

e.etymology: A respelling of Remi or Remy, the French form of Latin Remigius, traditionally derived from remex, oarsman. Saint Remigius was the bishop of Reims who baptized the Frankish king Clovis.
The Latin word lumen, light, which is also the scientific unit for the amount of light a source gives off. Its use as a given name is recent.

assoc.t: unit of brightness printed on light bulb packaging

e.etymology: The English word nation, from Latin natio, a people or birth, used as a modern word name. Nation is also an English surname.

A modern American spelling in the family of Zaire, Zyaire and Zyir. Zaire was the Portuguese name for the Congo River, from a Kikongo word for river, and the name of the country now called the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
A spelling of Elias, the Greek form of the Hebrew name Elijah, my God is Yahweh. This spelling follows the sound of the Arabic form Ilyas and the Ethiopian form of the prophet's name.
From Arabic hamdan, built on the root h-m-d, praise, which also gives Muhammad, Ahmad, Hamid and Mahmud. It is both a given name and a family name across the Arab world.
A respelling of Emerson, an English surname meaning son of Emery. Emery comes from a Germanic name whose second element is ric, ruler or power.
A respelling of Royalty, the English word for kings, queens and their rank, used as a given name in the US since the 2010s. Royal comes through Old French from Latin regalis, of a king.
The Hebrew word emunah, faith or trust, from the same root as amen. It is used as a girl's name mainly in Jewish families.
A recent American name with no recorded history of its own. It is close in spelling and sound to Nayeli, a Mexican name from the Zapotec language of Oaxaca.

A Japanese given name whose meaning depends on the characters used to write it. In English, mako is also a fast open-ocean shark, a word borrowed from Maori, and that is likely the sense behind most American use for boys.
namesakes: Mako (Japanese American actor, Oscar nominee for The Sand Pebbles)
Mako (firebender in the animated series The Legend of Korra)

assoc.t: mako shark, among the fastest sharks in the ocean
Mako, the firebender of The Legend of Korra

e.etymology: A Spanish name honoring the Virgin of Hope of Macarena, venerated in the Macarena district of Seville. The district's name is traced either to Greek makarios, blessed, or to an Arabic place name.

assoc.t: 1990s dance-craze song by Los del Rio

e.note: Most Americans will think first of the 1996 hit song and its line dance.

e.etymology: The English word reason, used as a modern word name; Reason is also an English surname. In 19th-century American records Reason often stands for Rezin, an Old Testament name said the same way.
The name of a powerful fighter in the anime Dragon Ball Super, introduced in 2017, just before the name peaked in the US. The character's name is a wordplay on renji, Japanese for a kitchen range.

assoc.t: Dragon Ball Super fighter from Universe 11

e.etymology: A recent American name that reads as Nova, Latin for new, with an added A- in the manner of Amora and Anora. It has no recorded history as a traditional name.

assoc.t: ANOVA, the statistics method analysis of variance

e.note: ANOVA is a standard term in statistics classes, and Anova is a brand of sous vide cookers.

e.etymology: A recent coinage in the pattern of Leilani and Kailani, whose -lani ending is the Hawaiian word for sky or heaven. The first part has no settled source.

A respelling of Callahan, the English form of the Irish surname O Ceallachain, descendant of Ceallachan. That personal name is a pet form of Ceallach, explained either as bright-headed or as contentious.
A spelling of Elaine, the Old French form of Helen, known from Arthurian legend as Elaine of Astolat. Helen is Greek and is often linked to a word for torch or light.
namesakes: Elayne Trakand (heroine of The Wheel of Time)

assoc.t: Elayne Trakand of The Wheel of Time
